ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Early feeding

A 44-year-old man with mild acute pancreatitis improves after initial treatment. He has no vomiting or ileus and wants to eat. His lipase is still elevated, but his pain is much better. Which nutritional approach is most appropriate?

  1. Fast until lipase is normal
  2. Use total parenteral nutrition routinely
  3. Avoid all nutrition for two weeks
  4. Give antibiotics instead of food
  5. Resume oral feeding as tolerated
Answer and explanation

Resume oral feeding as tolerated

Clinical tolerance, rather than normalization of lipase, guides resumption of oral intake.

Option explanations

Resume oral feeding as tolerated: Clinical tolerance, rather than normalization of lipase, guides resumption of oral intake.

Fast until lipase is normal: Enzyme normalization is not required before feeding.

Use total parenteral nutrition routinely: Parenteral nutrition is not needed when the gut is usable.

Avoid all nutrition for two weeks: Prolonged starvation is not the goal.

Give antibiotics instead of food: Antibiotics do not provide nutritional support.
